segments.text: For the questions below, complete the notes with a word or short phrase. You now have 30 seconds to look at the notes.
Hello Mr MacDonald, I understand you're here to have a lump removed from your back and
the plan is to send you home later today?
Yes, that's right.
The lump really needs to come off.
It's more than a little annoying and can be quite painful too.
It's right near my waist and gets in the way of the waistband and my trousers.
I'm not particularly worried about the surgery.
They explained everything to me very clearly when I was in the assessment clinic.
But I'm concerned about how I'll go on later when I'm recovering.
Did they tell you I have Parkinson's disease?
Yeah, it's here and you know it's from the clinic.
But it doesn't say how long you've had it or anything about how it affects you.
Oh, I've had it for a few years now.
Five, I think.
The walking is the worst.
It's difficult to start moving and I'm so slow.
All I can do is shuffle to start with and then my steps get shorter and shorter
and I get faster and faster.
Sometimes I even fall over.
Do you have any other physical problems?
I sometimes get the freezing thing that happens.
You know, where you're stuck in one spot.
A-kin-
A-kin-
A-kin-A-sia?
Yes, maybe.
You'd know better than me anyway.
It'll come on to me when I least expect it.
And it's always at the worst possible moment.
I've worked out that if I try to do more than one thing at once,
it almost always brings it on.
I also get this terrible shaking my hands.
It's hard to do something sometimes because my arms are so stiff.
What activities are most difficult for you?
It sounds ridiculous, but it's mainly things like turning over in bed,
reaching for a glass of water, getting up out of the chair and trying to turn around once I'm standing.
I've learned a few tricks to help along, like having a good firm mattress and a high-back chair with arms.
That's good. What about activities that need fine movements? How do you manage with those?
Well, tying my shoelaces is a real problem, and buttons. Doing up and undoing those things is almost impossible.
I like that material that sticks to itself, it's very handy. What's it called again? Velcro? That's it.
Also my hand-wresting is terrible. I've basically given up on it.
It really sounds like you might benefit from seeing an occupational therapist.
Yes, maybe. I'll have to speak to my GP about Ruffenil. One of the other major problems
I've had in the last 12 months has been the cramps I get at night. They really ruin my
sleep.
I understand your medication has been changed recently.
Yes, that's right. I said to the doctor that the cramps have gone on far too long, so she
said I should try some different tablets. I've only been taking them for a month or
so. I think they will really reduce the cramps.
Thank you.
